findings: CurvesExtend in full ETT generality is NOT proved and NOT stated. Conjectured counterexample (not formalized): the long ray with its order causality (local: locally the timelike line). Every curve over a real interval has sigma-compact image, bounded since omega_1 has uncountable cofinality, hence extensible: there is no inextensible curve at all, so CurvesExtend fails at any constant curve. The long ray is not second countable; whether CurvesExtend holds in every second countable or strongly causal spacetime is open.

Barbot's own GH definition (GHFspace.tex:502-504 (orig numbering)) asks exactly what the general theorem proves: curves extend to curves on which the time function is the parameter, onto t(M) = R. In ETT this is a theorem of GH + Geroch's hypotheses, not part of the definition.
questions: Should CurvesExtend remain a named hypothesis of IsCauchySurface.isAcausal / lemma K, or be replaced by the time-function hypothesis (or by the Geroch hypotheses, which every consumer already carries)? The time-function form is strictly more general than the GH form.

kb_proposals: Zorn over causal curves: do not order parametrised curves; order their IMAGES by inclusion, re-parametrised by a strict time function T (IsTimeGraph: T injective on K, invFunOn T K a curve over T(K)). The union of a chain is a time graph with no limit argument, and maximality is exactly DEC-13 inextensibility (CurvesExtend.lean).
